therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Type 2 diabetes patients inadequately controlled on metformin and a sulphonylurea
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: HbA1c change from baseline to week 24

biomarker_changes: FPG change from baseline to week 24: linagliptin -4.6 mg/dL vs placebo +8.1 mg/dL (difference -12.7 mg/dL, p<0.0001)
29.2% of linagliptin patients achieved HbA1c <7.0% vs 8.1% placebo (OR 5.510, p<0.0001)
13.1% of linagliptin patients achieved HbA1c <6.5% vs 4.2% placebo (OR 3.818, p<0.0001)
58.2% of linagliptin patients had HbA1c reduction ≥0.5% vs 30.2% placebo (OR 3.360, p<0.0001)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events were infrequent and similar between arms
Bone marrow failure reported in 1 linagliptin patient
Cardiac events (angina pectoris, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, myocarditis) reported in small numbers in both arms

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Linagliptin inhibits DPP-4 to raise GLP-1/GIP levels, enhancing incretin-mediated insulin secretion and complementing metformin's glucose-lowering biology through a distinct pathway
modulation_entries.citation: HbA1c change from baseline to week 24: linagliptin -0.72 vs placebo -0.10, mean difference -0.62 (95% CI: -0.73 to -0.50), p<0.0001
